breaking_changes: Version format changed from X.Y.Z (e.g., 11.9.0) to YYYY.WW.N (e.g., 2026.39.0); scripts or CI that parse --version output or the server startup log must be updated to match the new date-part scheme.

FLM model info registry_source in GET /pull/variants and GET /models responses is now an empty string for models without an explicit source instead of 'huggingface'; clients that assume the field always contains 'huggingface' or 'modelscope' will see '' and may misinterpret it.
The unversioned /docs route now returns a JSON 404 instead of falling through to the SPA web-app; anyone relying on /docs/example being silently served by the SPA will receive a 404.

evidence.blockers: Three items block shipping: the new release candidate publishing pipeline (GitHub prereleases and branch creation) has never been exercised end-to-end, the version format change affects all clients and scripts that parse version output, and the FLM API response encoding changed in a way that could break dependent clients. The wildcard origin security feature must also be verified before shipping.
evidence.breaking_changes: The version format shift (X.Y.Z → YYYY.WW.N) is a fundamental change to every artifact's identity string — CMake, MSI, Docker, and server output all emit the new format. Python3 is now a hard build dependency on Linux (added to CMake find_package, Dockerfile apt deps, and debian/control). The FLM API response for registry_source changed default from 'huggingface' to empty string, a subtle but real encoding shift. The unversioned /docs route now returns JSON 404 instead of SPA fallback, a deliberate fix for a UI leak.
evidence.coverage: All 41 commits were reviewed by the commit review pipeline. 21 to-dos carry across from those reviews; every to-do is represented in this checklist with a priority.
evidence.manual_testing: Human verification is needed for: (1) the new candidate release infrastructure — push to release-v* and confirm prereleases and Docker candidate tags are published correctly; (2) the wildcard origin matching — test that wildcard port and subdomain patterns behave securely; (3) the /pull/variants error path — confirm incompatible GGUF repos return 400 while valid ones return variants; (4) the new docs endpoints and MCP tool — exercise live and confirm correct responses; (5) the version format — confirm the new YYYY.WW.N output on the release candidate.
evidence.security: Wildcard origin matching (:) and subdomain pattern (*.domain) is a new security-sensitive feature — subdomain spoofing via loose matching would be a real vulnerability. The new session header relay uses a strict well-known-only allowlist and deliberately excludes telemetry headers. The /pull/variants architecture filter prevents downloading incompatible repos. The example HTML server docs need --bind 127.0.0.1 to avoid accidentally exposing file trees on all interfaces.
